items.title: Rockstar's custom GTA VI PS5 Pro consoles are giveaway-only — just 100 exist
items.summary: TweakTown reports Rockstar is giving away, not selling, at least 100 custom GTA VI PS5 Pro consoles — dark gray-and-black with etched palm trees, the GTA VI logo and neon teal-to-magenta accents, each carrying a unique serial number — first to Miami Heat players before launch and now to streamers and influencers such as Davy Jones, while the matching black and white limited-edition DualSense controllers are sold at retail for $84.99.

items.title: Players are hitting a game-breaking Chapter 3 soft lock
items.summary: Polygon reports a game-breaking Chapter 3 soft lock that can leave the character switch stuck on Lucia after the Missing Persons mission, blocking the Jason segment that follows — it is the most-viewed bug on the GTA6Bugs tracker. Workarounds include reloading a manual save from before the Port Gellhorn warehouse meeting and playing Dealer's Choice as Jason first, or trying another duo mission, calling Dunk, or robbing a store together before Raul's job; the Nov. 23 update did not fix it.

items.title: Snake owners are mad about how Dolores is kept
items.summary: Polygon reports snake owners are up in arms over Dolores, the pet snake in Jason and Lucia's Key Lento bungalow: a Reddit post with more than 92,000 likes blasts her tank for lacking a heat lamp and a water dish, opening the wrong way, and Jason feeding her without tongs — while other players argue a poorly kept snake is exactly in character for the household.

items.title: Rockstar explains why GTA VI dropped mission replay
items.summary: Kotaku reports Rockstar senior design director Scott Butchard explained why GTA VI has no mission replay: the team considered it early on, but replaying missions from outside the story felt alien and disconnected and diminished the choices players had made — so story missions are one-and-done, with reloading a manual save the only way back in.

items.title: Rockstar reveals the features cut from GTA VI
items.summary: TheGamer reports Rockstar North's Rob Nelson and Scott Mitchell told PC Games about features cut from GTA VI: tennis was built but scrapped for not meeting the studio's standard, cinema and theatre visits were dropped as not interactive enough, and crawling, safehouse furnishing and crafting were all considered and left out — while mini golf did make the final game.

items.title: Guide: disable advanced trackers by letting your partner drive
items.summary: Polygon explains a teamwork workaround for stolen keyless cars with advanced trackers, which normally alert police if you drive too slowly: break in with the key cloner but do not drive off, ask your partner to wait in the car, get into another vehicle, then ask them to follow you — the tracker never activates because you are not driving it, and you can regroup outside Randy's or a Pay 'N' Spray to sell or register it.

items.title: Guide: unlock GTA VI's good ending
items.summary: ScreenRant lists what the good ending requires before you trigger the finale at Abe's: $2 million banked, a Level 4 relationship between Jason and Lucia, a Professional or Hardened criminal rating, shooting Mendez after his boss fight, and choosing to swim for it when the ending choice comes — with chain-robbing Vice City banks suggested as the way to reach the $2 million. (Spoilers.)

items.title: Guide: complete The Final Flush for a permanent stamina upgrade
items.summary: TheGamer walks through the conspiracy side quest that starts by scanning the #NOFLUSHERS QR poster in the toilet on Corsair Key: meet Dr. Merle at Frank's Waffles in Vice City, follow his swallowed tracker to the sewage plant, open the secret chamber and get flushed yourself to earn a permanent stamina upgrade — then check the sealed bunker in Lummox County, code 3612, for a dark follow-up reveal.

items.title: GTA VI's painted-on tunnel keeps fooling drivers
items.summary: Kotaku reports players keep crashing at speed into a fake tunnel painted on a wall in Vice City's Decor District near Stockyard — a realistic mural, in the style of a Looney Tunes gag, that looks like a real tunnel entrance until the moment you hit it, with clips of the wrecks piling up on social media since launch.

items.title: Panini is turning GTA VI's in-game cards into real trading cards
items.summary: Push Square reports Panini is making real-life GTA VI trading cards in partnership with Rockstar, based on the game's fictional sports teams and the collectible cards players find around Leonida: 480 cards across 16 sets, sold in four-pack boxes with rare team-colour parallels to chase, due out in December with no price announced yet.

items.title: Why GTA VI's Chapter 1 chores make its ending hurt
items.summary: Polygon argues the early house chores — Jason fixing steps and a railing, buying groceries, painting and building furniture for Lucia's return — are what make the Chapter 1 ending land: masked attackers searching for the bag burn the home down around Lucia's fight, destroying the crib, the coffee table they built together and Jason's keepsakes, and leaving the couple in a Port Gellhorn motel. (Spoilers for Chapter 1.)

items.title: Inside GTA VI's fursuit ban and the Furverts rescue
items.summary: Kotaku explains Leonida's fursuit ban, the TV spots urging people to report furries and the hunters licensed to shoot them — and why the game itself is sympathetic rather than hostile: a roadside encounter lets you rescue a fox-suited character and drive members of the underground Furverts to safety, and Jason and Lucia can text that furries are misunderstood, though nothing stops a player choosing violence after collecting the reward.

items.title: Guide: flip your car back over by hand
items.summary: Polygon explains you cannot right a flipped vehicle from inside in GTA VI: get out, walk against its middle until the shove prompt appears, then hold Square on PS5 or X on Xbox until it is upright — it only works on fully upended cars, boats and larger vehicles, not planes, and not if an obstacle blocks the other side.

items.title: Guide: get your car out of the police impound
items.summary: Polygon outlines two ways to recover an impounded car: sneak into the lot and steal it back, then escape the police, or from Chapter 2 use the Scooter Bros app to pay a distance-based fee — an example $699 from Vice City to Port Gellhorn — or spend Premium daily credits.

items.title: Guide: reveal the whole Leonida map from the air
items.summary: Polygon recommends clearing Leonida's fog from the air in a plane or helicopter, ideally the fuel-efficient Mammoth Dodo seaplane found near coastal hangars, swapping aircraft when fuel runs low, checking fuel with down on the D-pad, and avoiding lingering over yellow-tinted restricted sites like Mile Zero Air Station and VCIA.
